blocks.text: Ridge Regression and Lasso Regression covered the two genuine ends of the regularization spectrum, keep every feature and shrink, versus automatically select a sparse subset. Elastic net directly asks the genuinely natural next question, why not combine both penalties together into a single technique, and delivers a real, literal answer, blending L1 and L2 regularization into one combined loss function.

This topic covers the combined penalty elastic net actually optimizes, the two genuine hyperparameters this technique introduces, a real, specific weakness plain Lasso has with correlated features that elastic net directly fixes, the l1_ratio spectrum connecting pure Ridge and pure Lasso as its two genuine extremes, and ElasticNetCV, the standard tool for automating the search across both hyperparameters at once.
1. The Combined Penalty Elastic Net Actually Optimizes

blocks.alt: An L1 penalty and an L2 penalty together form the combined penalty

blocks.text: Elastic net genuinely adds both penalties to the standard mean squared error loss at once, a genuine L1 portion, the sum of absolute coefficient values, and a genuine L2 portion, the sum of squared coefficient values, blended together according to a chosen mixing proportion. The overall strength of this combined penalty is still genuinely controlled by alpha, exactly as in both Ridge and Lasso individually.

This is genuinely a direct, literal combination, not a new, unrelated idea, everything covered in the two previous topics about L1 and L2 individually applies here too, elastic net simply lets both genuinely operate together in the same fitted model.
2. Two Genuine Hyperparameters Instead of One

blocks.alt: Elastic net is controlled by alpha for overall strength and l1_ratio for balance

blocks.text: Alpha genuinely controls the overall regularization strength, exactly the same real role it played in both Ridge and Lasso individually. l1_ratio is genuinely new here, controlling the mixing proportion between the two penalty types, how much of the combined penalty comes from the L1 portion versus the L2 portion.

This means tuning elastic net genuinely involves searching across two dimensions at once rather than one, a real, practical complication worth knowing about directly before reaching for this technique, covered concretely in the section on ElasticNetCV later in this topic.

blocks.text: 3. A Real, Specific Weakness Plain Lasso Has

blocks.alt: A group of correlated features leaves plain lasso picking just one

blocks.text: When several features are genuinely highly correlated with each other, plain Lasso tends to pick roughly one of them somewhat arbitrarily, driving its coefficient to a real, nonzero value while zeroing out the rest of that same correlated group entirely, even though all of them may genuinely carry similar, real signal. Which specific feature Lasso happens to keep can be genuinely sensitive to small, essentially arbitrary details in the data.

This is a genuinely real, practical weakness worth knowing about directly, plain Lasso automatic selection is not always genuinely stable or well reasoned when correlated features are involved, it can look confident while actually being somewhat arbitrary underneath.

blocks.title: Worth remembering
blocks.content: Plain Lasso genuine feature selection among a correlated group of features can be genuinely arbitrary, not a considered, stable choice. This is exactly the real weakness elastic net was built to address.

blocks.text: 4. How Elastic Net Directly Fixes This

blocks.alt: Elastic net keeps the whole group of correlated features instead of picking just one

blocks.text: The L2 portion of the combined elastic net penalty genuinely encourages correlated features to be treated together, similarly to how Ridge alone stabilizes them, while the L1 portion still genuinely drives truly irrelevant features to exactly zero. The real, practical result is a model that genuinely keeps a correlated group of real, useful features together with similar coefficients, rather than arbitrarily keeping just one, while still genuinely excluding features that carry no real signal at all.

This is genuinely the literal, real payoff promised at the start of this topic, Ridge stability for correlated features, combined directly with Lasso genuine sparsity for irrelevant ones, in a single, unified fitted model.
5. A Worked Example

blocks.alt: Correlated features fit with elastic net produce a balanced result

blocks.text: Fitting ElasticNet directly on a dataset with both a correlated group and a genuinely irrelevant feature shows this combined behavior in practice.

code.content:
from sklearn.linear_model import ElasticNet
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler
import pandas as pd

X = pd.DataFrame({
    "total_rooms": [3, 4, 5, 6, 7],
    "bedrooms_plus_baths": [3, 4, 5, 6, 7],
    "shoe_size_unrelated": [8, 9, 7, 10, 8],
})
y = pd.Series([250000, 310000, 360000, 410000, 460000])

X_scaled = StandardScaler().fit_transform(X)
model = ElasticNet(alpha=1.0, l1_ratio=0.5)
model.fit(X_scaled, y)

print(dict(zip(X.columns, model.coef_)))

blocks.text: total_rooms and bedrooms_plus_baths genuinely both keep meaningful, similar coefficients here, rather than one arbitrarily winning over the other, while shoe_size_unrelated genuinely still gets pulled toward zero, exactly the combined behavior this technique is built to deliver.

blocks.title: A practical habit
blocks.content: Scale features before fitting ElasticNet, exactly the same discipline established for Ridge and Lasso individually, since both the L1 and L2 portions of this combined penalty depend on comparable coefficient magnitudes.

blocks.text: 6. The l1_ratio Spectrum

blocks.alt: l1_ratio 0 is pure ridge while l1_ratio 1 is pure lasso

blocks.text: Setting l1_ratio to exactly 0 genuinely reduces elastic net down to plain Ridge regression, pure L2, no sparsity at all. Setting it to exactly 1 genuinely reduces it down to plain Lasso, pure L1. Every value genuinely in between produces a real, specific blend, both techniques covered so far in this module are genuinely just the two extreme endpoints of this same, single, unified elastic net spectrum.

This reframing is genuinely worth holding onto directly, Ridge and Lasso were never truly separate, unrelated algorithms, they are the two boundary cases of the more general elastic net family, now fully understood as one coherent, unified idea.

blocks.text: 7. ElasticNetCV: Automating Both Searches at Once

blocks.alt: Alpha and l1_ratio are tried together and cross validated to find the best combination

blocks.text: Manually tuning both alpha and l1_ratio by hand genuinely means searching across a two dimensional grid of candidates, considerably more involved than tuning either parameter alone. ElasticNetCV genuinely automates this entire combined search using cross validation, returning the empirically best performing combination of both hyperparameters directly.

This is genuinely the standard, practical way elastic net actually gets applied in a real project, letting a systematic, data driven search handle a genuinely two dimensional tuning problem that would be tedious and error prone to explore by hand.
8. Elastic Net Versus What Comes Next

Ridge, Lasso, and Elastic Net together close out the genuine regularized linear model family this course has built up step by step, penalized shrinkage, automatic sparsity, and now their genuine combination. Every one of these three techniques, though, shares one real, philosophical trait, they all work by directly penalizing large coefficients within the exact same least squares fitting framework.

The next topic, Bayesian Regression, introduces a genuinely different philosophy entirely, treating coefficients not as fixed numbers to penalize, but as genuinely uncertain quantities with their own probability distributions, a real, meaningful shift in how regression itself gets approached.

items: Elastic net genuinely combines the L1 and L2 penalties together into a single, unified loss function.
It genuinely introduces two hyperparameters, alpha for overall strength and l1_ratio for the L1 versus L2 mix.
Plain Lasso genuinely picks somewhat arbitrarily among correlated features, a real weakness elastic net fixes.
Elastic net genuinely keeps correlated features together while still zeroing out truly irrelevant ones.
l1_ratio at 0 is genuinely pure Ridge, at 1 is genuinely pure Lasso, with a real blend in between.
The next topic, Bayesian Regression, introduces a genuinely different, probabilistic approach to regression entirely.
